data.narrative:
Hyperscale Power is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Rothmund (PhD ETH Zurich, ex-ABB) and Sami Pettersson (ex-ABB), which has raised €5M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises 9 known private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, plus 1 public comparable (LNZA).

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression. Using the €5M total raised as a base value proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier for progression from Seed to the next institutional stage yields an implied valuation of €12M. The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables; while 9 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy simultaneous filters for stage, timing, and valuation tier. A reliance on broad-sector medians would introduce unwarranted noise given Hyperscale Power's specific positioning.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of €11M (low) to €14M (high), centered on €12M (median). This narrow range reflects methodological constraint rather than analytical confidence. Key uncertainties include the absence of true stage-matched peers in the dataset and limited visibility into Hyperscale Power's current unit economics, burn rate, and technology de-risking since the €5M raise. Further validation would require either additional comparable transactions or internal performance milestones.
